guide: Unit tests live in tests/ and are named test_*.py. They are unittest.TestCase classes that call the real textkit functions (never a re-implementation) and use plain unittest assertions. To write one, create tests/test_<name>.py with a class subclassing unittest.TestCase, add methods named test_*, and run python -m junit_runner tests test-results/unit.xml from the project directory (or .venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -v for verbose output). The runner discovers test_*.py under the given directory, writes JUnit XML to the report path, and exits non-zero on failure.
acceptance_guide: Acceptance tests live in acceptance/ and are named test_*.py. They meet the product the way its user does: through the public import contract (import textkit; call textkit.slugify / textkit.word_count / textkit.truncate / textkit.title_case) and through the documented examples as bare-call docstring doctests. To write one, create acceptance/test_<name>.py with a unittest.TestCase class (or plain function that raises on failure), import textkit inside it, and run python -m junit_runner acceptance test-results/acceptance.xml from the project directory. The runner discovers test_*.py under acceptance/, writes JUnit XML to the report path, and exits non-zero on failure. There is no server, database, or browser in this product - it is a stateless library - so the acceptance suite exercises pure functions and the import path only.
